properties.description: Hierapolis cemetery is one of the widest cemeteries in Anatolia. It has three different parts, north, south and west. The north one is the largest one in Hierapolis with more than 1200 graves.

Dedicated to Apollo Lairbenos, the town's principal god during the late Hellenistic period. The temple of Apollo was deliberately built over an active fault. This fault was called the Plutonion. It was the oldest religious centre of the native communi

properties.note: Path is a low slope rock face with lukewarm water running down it. In the winter, by the time the water reaches the bottom of the bath, it is freezing cold. Shoes must be removed or a different entrance to the top must be used.

properties.description: Built by the proconsul Julius Frontinus (84–86) -monumental entrance that leads onto the large plateia, 14 m wide, which crosses the whole settlement, exiting a gate at the opposite side, to connect with the road that goes to Laodicea on the Lykos

properties.description: The north gate forms part of a fortification system built at Hierapolis in Theodosian times (late 4th c) and is its monumental entrance. Built of reused material from the demolition of the Agora with apotropeic elements: Gorgon head

properties.description: Amid the remains of a fourth- or fifth-century church at Hierapolis, one of the most significant Christian sites in Turkey, Francesco D’Andria found this first-century Roman tomb that he believes once held the remains of the apostle Philip.
